Method

How this list was built

A working corpus, not a systematic review. One search, run in three databases on 2026-10-02.

Searches. The same terms in Web of Science Core Collection (984 records), Scopus (1,230) and PubMed (475): title, abstract and keywords, 2021–2026; musicians, music-industry workers or their job titles, crossed with mental-health, psychosocial-work and occupational-disease terms; music therapy, music listening, music-based or music interventions, dementia and stroke excluded. Deduplicated by DOI and title: 1,470.

The three queries

Web of Science: TS=((musician* OR "music industry" OR "music workers" OR "music sector" OR songwriter* OR composer* OR "music producer*" OR "record producer*" OR "recording engineer*" OR "mixing engineer*" OR "mastering engineer*" OR "sound engineer*" OR "audio engineer*" OR "live sound" OR "sound technician*" OR roadie* OR "road crew*" OR "touring crew*" OR "tour manager*" OR "artist manager*" OR "music manager*") AND ("mental health" OR depression OR anxiety OR wellbeing OR "well-being" OR "psychological distress" OR burnout OR suicide OR "occupational health" OR psychosocial OR "working conditions" OR precarious OR "occupational stress" OR "occupational disease" OR "occupational injury" OR "occupational injuries" OR "playing-related" OR "performance-related pain" OR musculoskeletal OR dystonia OR "overuse injury" OR "overuse injuries" OR "hearing loss" OR tinnitus OR "noise-induced" OR "work-related injury" OR "work-related injuries")) NOT TS=("music therapy" OR "music listening" OR "music-based" OR "music intervention" OR dementia OR stroke) AND PY=(2021-2026)

Scopus: TITLE-ABS-KEY((musician* OR "music industry" OR "music workers" OR "music sector" OR songwriter* OR composer* OR "music producer*" OR "record producer*" OR "recording engineer*" OR "mixing engineer*" OR "mastering engineer*" OR "sound engineer*" OR "audio engineer*" OR "live sound" OR "sound technician*" OR roadie* OR "road crew*" OR "touring crew*" OR "tour manager*" OR "artist manager*" OR "music manager*") AND ("mental health" OR depression OR anxiety OR wellbeing OR "well-being" OR "psychological distress" OR burnout OR suicide OR "occupational health" OR psychosocial OR "working conditions" OR precarious OR "occupational stress" OR "occupational disease" OR "occupational injury" OR "occupational injuries" OR "playing-related" OR "performance-related pain" OR musculoskeletal OR dystonia OR "overuse injury" OR "overuse injuries" OR "hearing loss" OR tinnitus OR "noise-induced" OR "work-related injury" OR "work-related injuries")) AND PUBYEAR > 2020 AND PUBYEAR < 2027 AND NOT TITLE-ABS-KEY("music therapy" OR "music listening" OR "music-based" OR "music intervention" OR dementia OR stroke)

PubMed: ((musician*[tw] OR "music industry"[tw] OR "music workers"[tw] OR "music sector"[tw] OR songwriter*[tw] OR composer*[tw] OR "music producer*"[tw] OR "record producer*"[tw] OR "recording engineer*"[tw] OR "mixing engineer*"[tw] OR "mastering engineer*"[tw] OR "sound engineer*"[tw] OR "audio engineer*"[tw] OR "live sound"[tw] OR "sound technician*"[tw] OR roadie*[tw] OR "road crew*"[tw] OR "touring crew*"[tw] OR "tour manager*"[tw] OR "artist manager*"[tw] OR "music manager*"[tw]) AND ("mental health"[tw] OR depression[tw] OR anxiety[tw] OR wellbeing[tw] OR "well-being"[tw] OR "psychological distress"[tw] OR burnout[tw] OR suicide[tw] OR "occupational health"[tw] OR psychosocial[tw] OR "working conditions"[tw] OR precarious[tw] OR "occupational stress"[tw] OR "occupational disease"[tw] OR "occupational injury"[tw] OR "occupational injuries"[tw] OR "playing-related"[tw] OR "performance-related pain"[tw] OR musculoskeletal[tw] OR dystonia[tw] OR "overuse injury"[tw] OR "overuse injuries"[tw] OR "hearing loss"[tw] OR tinnitus[tw] OR "noise-induced"[tw] OR "work-related injury"[tw] OR "work-related injuries"[tw])) NOT ("music therapy"[tw] OR "music listening"[tw] OR "music-based"[tw] OR "music intervention"[tw] OR dementia[tw] OR stroke[tw]) AND 2021:2026[dp] — PubMed holds no record with "music workers", "record producer*", "mastering engineer*", "road crew*", "touring crew*", "artist manager*", "music manager*", so those phrases add nothing there.

Screening. Of the 1,470, 176 had already been removed with a reason and 256 were rows from the 2026-09-12 and 2026-10-01 searches (253 rows; 3 carry a second DOI). 1,038 had never been screened: 269 left on record type (book chapters, books, conference papers, meeting abstracts, letters, editorials); the other 769 were read at abstract level against the scope below — 274 added, 492 removed, 3 held back until the full text can be read. Every verdict given with less than high confidence, plus 40 chosen at random from the rest, was screened again blind; the 41 disagreements were decided by hand. The 4 pre-2021 background anchors sit outside the search’s years; earlier rows this search does not retrieve were removed.

What counts as in scope. The two SPIDER axes of this field’s spine scoping review: the sample must be musicians or music-industry workers, the phenomenon their own mental health, occupational health or psychosocial work environment. Then two rules of this project’s own: student- and music-teacher-sample studies are out (mixed samples that also contain professionals stay, tagged Mixed, so a student sub-group can still be present there), and only peer-reviewed journal articles are in, judged on the record type.

Two tag columns. Study type is the article’s form; population is the sample it studies. Both are rule-assigned from title and abstract, except 19 typed by hand from the full text or the abstract’s method detail, marked ● hand-typed with the evidence. Where the evidence is absent the cell reads Undetermined or Unstated rather than guessing. There is no topic column: one topic label cannot be assigned from a title and abstract without discarding most of what a record is about.

Job titles are a sub-tag, and mostly empty — which is the finding. Where a record names the role it studies, that role is tagged under the population, and a record can carry more than one. The zeros in the table are not a tagging artefact: across the whole corpus crew, roadie appear in no title or abstract at all, engineer in 5, technician in 2, composer in 4, songwriter in 1, producer in 6. Nor are they a search artefact: the query names these job titles itself.

Tiers and abstracts. Cited — 11 rows whose PDF is held and which the overview cites. Held — 31 whose PDF is held but uncited; held means the file is there, not that it was read. Screened — 489 with no PDF: not read, not appraised. 497 rows carry the authors’ own abstract verbatim (122 Crossref, 236 Web of Science, 110 Scopus, 26 PubMed, 3 from a PDF held here); nothing there is written or translated by this project, so a few are in the article’s original language.

Provenance

Where every field comes from

  • Titles, authors, journals, years — the Web of Science export of 2026-09-12, completed from the Crossref REST API. The export’s abstract and times-cited columns came back empty, so neither is used.
  • Abstracts — Crossref publisher deposits, PubMed, or the PDF held here. Stated per row.
  • DOIs and open-access locations — Crossref, the NCBI ID Converter and Unpaywall.
  • Study type, population, the screening rule and the tiers — this project’s own work, described above; not from any database.
  • Not searched — PsycInfo, Chinese-language indexes (華藝, TCI-HSS), grey literature.
